column7: Follow-up of #3361 for the role->permission cache generation (REVIEW-FIXES-1). The generation proof (rolePermGenerationTriggersPresentExpr) accepted any trigger with tgenabled <> D and did not read session_replication_role, so a trigger in ENABLE REPLICA (never fires for an ordinary write) or an ordinary trigger skipped by a replica-role writer still passed, and a permission removed by direct SQL kept authorizing from a warm cache. The proof now uses the cache-epoch proof condition (pgTriggerFiresForEveryWriter: tgenabled = A and an origin session); the migration re-issues ENABLE ALWAYS for every other state. Also TestRolePermissionGeneration_OrdinaryTriggerSkippedByReplicaWriter_Postgres and _ProofFailsClosedInReplicaSession_Postgres. Red on main: the proof reported R/O triggers and a replica session as present, and the warm cache authorized a removed permission.
